newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels seize Zaire town, extend their advance.
newsitem.headline: Rebels seize Zaire town, extend their advance.

text.p: Rebels have captured the east Zaire town of Shabunda and are advancing towards Kindu where the army massed troops before launching its counter-offensive last month, church sources and aid workers said on Thursday.

The rebels, who have frustrated the army offensive by opening up new fronts, were advancing west in large numbers on Kindu, with its army base and airport around 200 km (125 miles) to the west, the sources in the region added.
The sources said that the town fell on Wednesday. Up to 40,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees fled west into the forest earlier after reports that the Tutsi-led rebels had taken a nearby town.
One source said that soldiers from Zaire's demoralised army fled through the town on Tuesday and that local people gathered in a church and welcomed the arrival of the rebels.

Further north, on the road from the rebel-held east to Kisangani, headquarters of the counter offensive the army launched on January 20, relief workers spoke of a movement of people from the Amisi refugee camp 80 km (50 miles) from the town of Lubutu but had no details on the reason.
They said that Tingi Tingi refugee camp near Lubutu, which is 200 km (125 miles) from Kisangani, was calm.
